findings: Verified: _git_show_bytes distinguishes GIT_OBJECT_UNAVAILABLE (recoverable; fetch the bound object) from GIT_PATH_UNAVAILABLE, and binding content is checked only after a successful read — a missing object can no longer disprove an approval. Governance rows referencing unavailable commits fail registry validation loudly, withholding all completion authority (fail-closed).

Verified: fetch_provenance.py enforces a closed bounded manifest (full 40-hex commit, path locked to ideas/NNN/HUMAN_APPROVED_PROBE, 64-hex sha256, ≤16 entries), refuses the contaminated commit, fetches only exact SHAs at depth 1 with --filter=blob:none, and byte-verifies retrieved markers. Credential-helper config is also passed on `git show`, so the lazy promisor blob fetch inherits it. Workflow keeps contents:read and persist-credentials:false; no branch checkout/merge/push.

Verified: authority reads go only through mechanically_verified_ratifications; superseded rows (old registry bytes) confer nothing without erroring; current-bytes rows re-prove marker hashes, contract bindings, and import bundle manifests at read time. check_pilot_publication.py permits neither HUMAN_APPROVED_PROBE nor governance_events.jsonl paths on outgoing commits and confirms the contaminated commit is unreachable, so ratification rows cannot be forged via the outgoing branch.

Verified: state.json updates for 023/045/046 are internally consistent (registry.file_sha256 == materialization.sources.registry_sha256; approval/contract blobs coherent); only idea_card_sha256 and derived source_fingerprint_sha256 changed per the correction doc; approval and governance byte hashes unchanged.

MINOR (hardening): contract-binding checks are substring matches — verify_ratification_event uses `('contract_blob: ' + blob) in raw` and _attested_hashes uses an unanchored regex, so a marker line like `revoked_contract_blob: <X>` would falsely attest X. Anchor to line start (re.MULTILINE '^contract_blob:'). Bounded today because markers are review-controlled and immutable on the outgoing branch.

MINOR (hardening): _HEX7TO40 lets REGISTRY_RATIFIED rows bind abbreviated commit ids. Bindings are byte-pinned by approval_sha256 so prefix ambiguity there is contained, but imports bind source_commit only by prefix plus textual pin (no byte hash of the source marker), making a short prefix the weakest identity link. Require full 40-hex in governance rows, matching fetch_provenance's stricter manifest rule.

MINOR (observability): state_summary emits only approval_bound (marker binds current registry bytes), so the persisted views show approval_bound:false with all nodes COMPLETE when authority comes via verified ratification. Add a ratified_bound (or authority_source) field so audit artifacts distinguish ratified authority from no authority.
NIT: derive_status emits RESULT_PRESENT, which is absent from the module docstring's closed status/precedence list (STALE, COMPLETE, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, UNSTARTED) — document it.

NIT: artifact_issues resolves a consumed output against the repo root when the producing node declares no results_bundle (join with ''); validation does not require artifact-dep sources to declare results_bundle. Effectively fail-closed (declared sha256 must still match) but the resolution target is surprising — add a validator check that artifact-dep source nodes declare results_bundle.

NIT: terminal_statuses_if_approved matches bundles by path suffix (b.endswith('/'+rb)), so an absolute path outside the repo ending in the registry rel path is treated as that node's bundle; comparing resolved Path(root)/rb against the resolved bundle path would be stricter. Low risk since callers pass repo-local bundles.

NIT: _git_show_bytes attributes a `git cat-file` timeout to `git show` in its TimeoutExpired message; _canonical_rel accepts '.' (a results_bundle of the repo root passes validation); _dir_manifest_sha follows symlinks when hashing imported bundles.
